## Statements

- Stated by vendor (anthropic-opus-4-8-prompting, Calibrating effort and thinking depth): Start at xhigh for coding and agentic work and use high as the floor for intelligence-sensitive tasks. Effort is respected strictly, so low can under-think moderately complex work.
- Stated by vendor (anthropic-opus-4-8-prompting, Calibrating effort and thinking depth, Note): At xhigh or max effort, set a large output token budget, starting near 64k, so the model has room to think and act across subagents and tool calls.
- Stated by vendor (anthropic-opus-4-8-prompting, Calibrating effort and thinking depth, line 47): Thinking stays off unless a request sets adaptive thinking. If it thinks too often with large system prompts, prompt to respond directly when reasoning would not help.
- Stated by vendor (anthropic-deprecations, API parameter deprecations table, temperature/top_p/top_k row): Leave temperature, top_p and top_k unset; non-default values return a 400. For design variety, have it propose several directions before building.
- Stated by vendor (anthropic-opus-4-8-prompting, Code review harnesses): Review prompts that say to report only important issues are followed literally and lower recall. Ask for every finding with confidence and severity, and filter in a later step.
- Stated by vendor (anthropic-opus-4-8-prompting, More literal instruction following): It reads prompts literally and does not generalize an instruction to other items. State the scope you want, such as every section, when the rule should apply broadly.
- Stated by vendor (anthropic-opus-4-8-prompting, Tool use triggering): It favors reasoning over tool calls. Raise effort to high or xhigh, or say when and how to use tools, when a task needs more searching or tool use.
- Stated by vendor (anthropic-opus-4-8-prompting, Controlling subagent spawning): It spawns fewer subagents by default. Say when to delegate and when to work directly, for example fan out across many files in one turn.
- Stated by vendor (anthropic-opus-4-8-prompting, User-facing progress updates): It gives regular progress updates on long runs. Remove scaffolding that forces interim summaries, and describe the format you want if the default is off.
- Stated by vendor (anthropic-opus-4-8-prompting, Interactive coding products): It spends more tokens in multi-turn interactive sessions because it reasons after each user turn. Put task, intent and constraints in the first turn to save tokens.
- Stated by vendor (anthropic-opus-4-8-prompting, Design and frontend defaults): Its default UI style is cream backgrounds, serif type and a terracotta accent. Give a concrete palette and typography instead of a generic instruction like clean and minimal.
- Stated by vendor (anthropic-opus-4-8, Page header and Availability table): Opus 4.8 is a legacy model; Anthropic points to Opus 5.5 as the current Opus. It stays active, with retirement not sooner than May 28, 2027.
- Stated by vendor (anthropic-effort, Recommended effort levels for Claude Opus 5): Effort defaults to high. Treat low and medium as the main cost and latency controls where evals hold, and use xhigh for demanding coding and agentic work. Re-run the sweep when carrying settings from another model.
- Stated by vendor (anthropic-opus-5-prompting, Response length and verbosity; User-facing progress updates; Written deliverable length): Effort changes thinking volume, not reply length, so ask for brevity in the prompt. It narrates readily during agentic work and writes longer files than earlier Opus; describe the update cadence and length you want.
- Stated by vendor (anthropic-opus-5-prompting, Task scope and over-verification; Controlling subagent spawning; Self-correction): It verifies and corrects its own work, so lines asking for extra verification or double-checks add cost without gain. It can also widen scope and delegate readily: bound the task and cap subagents.
- Stated by vendor (anthropic-opus-5-prompting, Running with thinking disabled): Thinking is on by default and can be disabled only at high effort or below; xhigh and max return 400. With it off, tool calls can leak into reply text, so prefer thinking on at low effort.
- Stated by vendor (anthropic-opus-5-prompting, Reasoning in the response): Asking it to write out its reasoning in the reply can be declined as a reasoning_extraction refusal. Ask for a short explanation, or keep thinking on and read summarized thinking blocks.
- Stated by vendor (anthropic-opus-5, Page header and Availability table): Opus 5 is a legacy model; Opus 5.5 is the current Opus, which the opus alias reaches. Opus 5 stays active, with retirement not sooner than July 24, 2027. Pin claude-opus-5 by name for Opus 5.
- Stated by harness (cc-model-config, Model aliases, provider table): In Claude Code the opus alias reaches Opus 5.5 on the Anthropic API, Platform on AWS, Bedrock and Agent Platform; only Foundry still reaches Opus 4.6. Pin claude-opus-4-8 by name for Opus 4.8.
- Stated by vendor (anthropic-opus-5-5-prompting, Calibrate effort): Effort defaults to medium and a request without it runs a level below Opus 5. Set it explicitly; medium matches Opus 5 at high on coding evals. Re-run sweeps, as levels are recalibrated.
- Stated by vendor (anthropic-opus-5-5-whats-new, Thinking can't be disabled): Thinking is always on. Disabled and manual budget_tokens return 400, as do forced tool use and non-default temperature, top_p or top_k. Steer cost with effort.
- Stated by vendor (anthropic-opus-5-5-prompting, Calibrate effort): It thinks more per turn than Opus 5 at the same effort, most at xhigh and max. Reserve those for measured gains and set max_tokens high, up to 128000 for agentic coding.
- Stated by vendor (anthropic-opus-5-5-prompting, Unattended agentic runs): On long unattended runs it may end a turn with text and no tool call. Treat that as a report, track open items in a checklist, and name the early stops to avoid in the system prompt.
- Stated by vendor (anthropic-opus-5-5-whats-new, Behavior differences, text between tool calls): Notes between tool calls arrive as thinking blocks, empty under the default display, so a client showing only text goes quiet. Set display updates to render them.
- Stated by vendor (anthropic-opus-5-5-prompting, Prompts written for thinking disabled): Do not ask it to write out its reasoning in the reply; that can be declined as a reasoning_extraction refusal. Read summarized thinking blocks instead.
- Stated by vendor (anthropic-opus-5-5-whats-new, Thinking blocks are tied to the model and the conversation): Thinking blocks are bound to the model and conversation. Editing earlier turns or the system prompt can make replayed blocks fail with a 400, so keep history append-only.
